svg.text: Figure 2.3. WFI and wake: the down-counters, the local wake and the done gate
v1.0 (spec/machine-spec.md §4.12, §4.13, §6.3, §8) — one tile; every register clocks on the tile clock
A. A down-counter: DMA_SRAM_REMAINING shown; DMA_CM_REMAINING and DMA_REPLY_REMAINING are the same (§4.12, §8.7)
Next state: st ? wdata : (dec ? max(Q − 1, 0) : Q).
unexp = dec & (Q = 0): an arrival is judged against the
old count, then a same-cycle store overwrites it, and
An arrival at 0 holds 0 rather than wrapping.
a count of 0 never makes an edge:
wake = go_q | local-wake Q. GO enters through one register, go_q:
a GO pulse at t wakes a waiting WFI at t + 1.
A latch set at the end of cycle c releases a waiting WFI in c + 1:
its next instruction executes that cycle (panel E).
One wake consumes the local-wake latch; a WFI issued with the
latch already set falls straight through.
The done gate: from the done pulse until GO the latch cannot be set,
and the done pulse clears it, so only GO wakes wait_for_command().
Clears: a counter store, consume, the done pulse, halt; a clear wins
over a set in the same cycle.
A synchronised start uses identical code from WFI to the
start store on every tile (§6.3, figure 2.1).
D. The done gate, WFI control and the conditions (§4.12, §4.13, §6.3)
done is set by the done pulse, cleared by GO,
forced to 1 in HALT and cleared on entering
RUN; so done & RUN is exactly "from the done
pulse until GO", and the gate is 0 in HALT.
wake = GO | local_latch. A waiting WFI's next instruction
executes in the first cycle wake = 1: GO at t → t + 1 through go_q;
a latch set at the end of c → c + 1. One wake consumes the latch;
a WFI issued with it set falls straight through.
Done early tests the counters, not their idle bits.
E. Cycle timing (§4.12): a latch set at the end of cycle c releases a waiting WFI in c + 1; a late WFI falls through
(i) the last packet lands while the core waits
(ii) the copy ends first; the WFI comes late
(i) The last counted packet (here mode 5, DMA_CM_REMAINING) is accepted at t+1: the count reads 0 from t+2, and its port-B write is in flight until cm_idle returns at t+4.
all_done rises there, a qualified edge sets the latch at the end of t+4, and in t+5 its Q releases the waiting WFI. (ii) The latch holds the edge; the WFI at t+4 finds it set and falls through.
F. Interface: what the wake logic takes and drives
a store to that counter this cycle (st_cnt = st_S | st_C | st_R)
the store's data for the counters
a store with DMA_PULSE [0] set (start acts first, then done)
a counted packet accepted this cycle: mode match and src ≠ 64 (figure 5.1)
the big-SRAM write path is empty; the port-B pipeline is empty (§4.1, §4.12)
GO: one-cycle pulse, the same cycle on every tile; halt = ¬RUN
the WFI instruction executes this cycle
hold the core in WFI this cycle
DMA_SRAM_, DMA_CM_ and DMA_REPLY_REMAINING for loads (the value at the end of the previous cycle)

• Reset and HALT: the latch, the qualifier and the gate are 0 (halt is in every clear), which covers "cleared on HALT → RUN". On entering RUN no counter is set, so nothing can make an edge before the first
• The done gate blocks only the latch's set term; GO goes, through go_q, straight to the wake OR, so GO always wakes. The done pulse also clears the latch and the qualifier, so nothing leaks into
• In the latch and the qualifier a clear beats a set in the same cycle: each of their clears (a counter store, consume, the done pulse, halt) wins over an edge.
junction (crossings without a dot don't connect); wedge: clocked register
WFI wakes on GO or on the local wake: the latched edge of all three counters done, qualified by a counter having been non-zero. One wake
consumes the latch. From the done pulse until GO the gate holds the latch's set term off, so only GO can wake wait_for_command(). Counter
stores, consume, the done pulse and HALT clear the latch; a clear wins over a set in the same cycle.
